messages:
mira: Heads up — trying to onboard the new sampleapp with ephemeral tokens via the JS SDK and it fails during the first API call. curl against the REST endpoint with the same token works fine.

devon: hmm, any error logs? status code?

mira: 401 unauthorized from the SDK call. No body in the SDK error besides 'Unauthorized'. From curl I get 200 and the expected model list.

sam: can you paste the minimal repro?

mira: sure. repro steps: 1) mint ephemeral token from /v1/tokens on the server 2) pass it to client sampleapp (js sdk) 3) call client.models.list() -> 401.

mira: code:```js
// using @redwood/sdk client
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: EPHEMERAL_TOKEN });
await client.models.list(); // -> throws 401 Unauthorized
```

andre: interesting. does the browser send the token in Authorization header or as query param? some of the SDK wrappers rewrite headers for SSR safety.

mira: header: `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` — inspected in network tab. header is present.

devon: @mira can you try the raw fetch in the same environment as the sdk to rule out CORS/credential differences? e.g.:```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }})
```

mira: did that in the same page — fetch returns 200. so it's something the SDK is doing client-side pre-request (maybe adding x-client or changing path).

ci-bot: Deploy 2026-03-22T17:20:50Z succeeded on branch/sdk-client-headers (build #5821) :rocket:

sam: could be retry/auth middleware treating ephemeral tokens as stale and attempting a refresh flow (which returns 401) — SDK might be trying to call the admin refresh endpoint which requires a longer-lived key.

andre: good theory. @devon can you check SDK middleware behavior for 401 handling? particularly anything that auto-refreshes tokens or swaps to an internal admin route.

devon: on it. quick check: the client has an `authShim` that falls back to `/internal/refresh` when it sees 401 during model list. That path expects service token; not allowed for ephemeral tokens. I think the shim should only run for persisted keys.

mira: that matches what I saw — network trace shows a second request to `/internal/refresh` after the initial 401. server rejects that because ephemeral tokens aren't permitted there.

sam: fix: condition the authShim on `token_type !== 'ephemeral'` or add explicit header `x-skip-auth-shim`. also add a clearer error message in the SDK if an ephemeral token triggers that path.

andre: can someone open a tiny PR? change is small: guard the shim and modify error to `Ephemeral tokens cannot be refreshed; stop automatic refresh attempts` and include link to docs.

mira: filing issue now: #5123 — attaching network snip and stack trace. cc @devon @andre

devon: i'll add the unit test and a short e2e repro using the sampleapp. will aim for patch today.

sam: nice catch. also suggest we add a one-liner in onboarding docs about ephemeral tokens + SDK: `If using ephemeral tokens in browser, prefer fetch or set SDK flag { allowRefresh: false }` until patch ships.

mira: thanks! :thumbsup:

andre: note for release notes: this will be a behavior parity/compat fix — REST worked, SDK did auto-refresh which broke ephemeral flow. mark as bugfix and include migration section.

mira: closing loop — workaround for now: use direct fetch or set `process.env.REDWOOD_SDK_ALLOW_REFRESH=false` in sampleapp. we'll update the quickstart afterwards.

sam: great. leaving a reminder to audit other SDKs (python, go) for similar shim behavior.

mira: yep — creating followup ticket for multi-sdk audit.
